tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Required unless `stop` is true.

Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. - "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

12	
13	## 2. 前置知识
14	
15	### 2.1 魔数（magic number）
16	
17	文件的后缀名是可以随便改的：把 `photo.png` 改名成 `photo.pdf`，文件内容一个字节都不会变。所以判断文件真实类型的可靠办法，是读文件开头的几个字节——几乎所有文件格式都在开头约定了一串「签名字节」，俗称魔数：
18	
19	| 格式 | 开头字节（Python 字节串表示） | 长度 |
20	| --- | --- | --- |
21	| PNG | `b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"` | 8 字节 |
22	| JPEG | `b"\xff\xd8"`（SOI 段标记） | 2 字节 |
23	| PDF | `b"%PDF"` | 4 字节 |
24	
25	本讲会看到 olmOCR 对同一路径做了**后缀 + 魔数**的双重校验：后缀决定「要不要看」，魔数决定「算不算数」。
26	
27	### 2.2 glob 模式
28	
29	glob 是 shell 风格的通配符匹配：`*` 匹配任意字符序列，`?` 匹配单个字符，`[abc]` 匹配方括号内任一字符。`s3://bucket/pdfs/*.pdf` 的含义就是「该 bucket 下 pdfs 前缀里所有以 `.pdf` 结尾的对象」。S3 本身不支持通配符查询，所以代码需要先算出通配符之前的最长固定前缀，用前缀列举对象，再在客户端逐个做 glob 匹配。
30	
31	### 2.3 tarball 与 `tarball::内部路径` 记法
32	
33	tarball 指打包压缩文件（这里是 `.tar.gz` / `.tgz`）。olmOCR 允许把成百上千个 PDF 打成一个 tarball 交给流水线，用它自己的记法 `tarball路径::内部成员路径`（注意是**双冒号**）来指称「某个 tarball 里的某个 PDF」，例如 `s3://bucket/batch1.tar.gz::docs/paper.pdf`。这样做的好处是：百万个小文件在 S3 上列举、请求的开销都很大，合并成大对象能显著降低请求成本。
34

38	
39	\[ \bar{p} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i \]
40	
41	估计全体平均页数，再换算出每个工作项（work item group）应装多少篇文档。直觉是：**流水线真正的工作量以「页」为单位**（每页要渲染一次、推理一次），一个组装 5 篇 200 页的大书和装 5 篇 1 页的传单，工作量差了两个数量级。按页数定组大小，能让每个 work item 的工作量大致均匀，从而断点续跑的粒度均匀、重试的代价可控。

166	### 4.2 图片格式探测与图片转 PDF
167	
168	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
169	
170	olmOCR 的推理单元是「PDF 的一页」——渲染成图片交给视觉语言模型（u2-l3 会精读渲染）。既然模型看到的本来就是图片，那直接吃 PNG/JPEG 岂不更直接？流水线仍选择**先把图片包成单页 PDF**，理由是统一内部表示：下游所有环节（按页处理、页码元数据、Dolma 的 `pdf_page_spans`、断点重试）都建立在「文档 = 若干页」的抽象上。把图片包装成 1 页 PDF，就能让图片输入免费复用整套 PDF 机制，而不是在几十处代码里写 `if 图片` 分支。
171	
172	负责这件事的是 `olmocr/image_utils.py`，三个函数各司其职：`is_png`/`is_jpeg` 探测格式，`convert_image_to_pdf_bytes` 完成转换。
173	
174	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
175	
176	转换本身不重写 PDF 编码，而是调用外部命令行工具 `img2pdf`（「无损嵌入」：图片字节被直接放进 PDF 容器，不二次压缩）：
177	
178	```text
179	convert_image_to_pdf_bytes(路径或路径列表)
180	  ├─ 输入归一化: str → [str]; 空列表 → ValueError
181	  ├─ 逐个检查文件存在, 不存在 → ValueError
182	  ├─ subprocess.run(["img2pdf", 文件...], capture_output=True)
183	  │    ├─ 成功 → 返回 stdout (即 PDF 字节)
184	  │    └─ CalledProcessError → 抛 RuntimeError(携带 stderr)
185	```
186	
187	在流水线中的消费时机（不是收集时立刻转，而是**worker 取到文件时**才转）：
188	
189	```text
190	process_pdf(pdf_orig_path)
191	  ├─ get_s3_bytes_with_backoff 下载字节到临时文件 (本地路径则直接读盘)
192	  ├─ is_png(tf.name) 或 is_jpeg(tf.name)?
193	  │    └─ 是 → tf.seek(0); 重写为 convert_image_to_pdf_bytes(tf.name) 的输出
194	  └─ process_single_pdf(...)  # 此时临时文件一定是合法 PDF
195	```

293	### 4.3 pages_per_group 采样估算：按页定组
294	
295	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
296	
297	回忆 u1-l5：`--pages_per_group` 用 `argparse.SUPPRESS` 声明、无静态默认值，在 [pipeline.py:L1314-L1315](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1314-L1315) 按运行形态补默认：走外部计费 API（给了 `--api_key`）时目标是每组约 **50** 页，自有 GPU 时 **500** 页。本模块讲这个「目标页数」如何变成「每组文档数」。
298	
299	为什么按页分组（2.4 节的直觉再推一步）：一个 work item group 是断点续跑与完成标记的最小单元（u3-l1），组的工作量 = 组内总页数。若按固定文档数分组，遇到「1000 页的大书 + 1 页的收据」混合语料，组工作量会相差三个数量级：大组失败重试代价高、done flag 粒度太粗；小组则索引条目爆炸。控制「每组页数恒定」→ 每组重试代价上限恒定、进度统计均匀。
300	
301	#### 4.3.2 核心流程
302	
303	```text
304	若 pdf_work_paths 非空:
305	  n = min(100, 文档总数)
306	  sampled = random.sample(pdf_work_paths, n)        # 均匀随机抽样
307	  for pdf in sampled:
308	    字节 = get_s3_bytes(pdf_s3, pdf)                 # 本地路径直接读盘, s3 路径走网络
309	    写入临时文件
310	    if is_png 或 is_jpeg: 页数 = 1
311	    else:               页数 = len(PdfReader(临时文件).pages)
312	    读取失败 → warning 并跳过 (不中断)
313	  平均页数 p̄ = sum(页数) / len(页数)   # 全部失败 → 兜底 p̄ = 10
314	  items_per_group = max(1, int(pages_per_group / p̄))
315	  populate_queue(pdf_work_paths, items_per_group)
316	```
317	
318	换算公式（`int()` 即向零取整，也就是正数域的下取整 \(\lfloor\cdot\rfloor\)）：
319	
320	\[ \text{items\_per\_group} = \max\left(1,\ \left\lfloor \frac{\text{pages\_per\_group}}{\bar{p}} \right\rfloor\right) \]
321	
322	几个边界：样本上限 100（再多的抽样收益递减，而每个样本都要下载一次文件）；单次读取失败只 warning 不中断（脏数据在大规模语料中是常态）；`max(1, ...)` 保证平均页数超过目标页数（比如全是 600 页的大书、目标 500 页）时，每组至少仍装 1 篇——宁可组偏大，也不能出现空组。

351	```
352	
353	全部样本读不出来时兜底 \(\bar{p}=10\)——一个「typical 文档十页上下」的经验值，保证流程能继续。最后 [pipeline.py:L1408](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1408) 把结果交给 `populate_queue`；而 tarball 走的是 [pipeline.py:L1411-L1412](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1411-L1412) 的独立通道——`populate_queue(tarball_paths, 1)`，**一个 tarball 就是一个工作项**，不参与页数估算（tarball 内部 PDF 由 `process_tarball` 在 worker 阶段整体解开，见 [pipeline.py:L485-L503](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L485-L503)，成员以 `tarball::成员名` 记法登记）。
354	
355	代一个小数：若采样得 \(\bar{p}=8.2\)、自有 GPU 默认目标 500 页，则 \(\lfloor 500/8.2 \rfloor = 60\)，每组约 60 篇文档；若走 API 默认 50 页，则 \(\lfloor 50/8.2 \rfloor = 6\)。同一个语料，两种运行形态的组粒度差 10 倍——这就是 u1-l5 说「走计费 API 要调小闸门」在分组侧的体现。
356	
357	#### 4.3.4 代码实践
358	
359	**实践目标**：复刻采样估算，用仓库自带的「困难 PDF」当语料，感受 \(\bar{p}\) 对 `items_per_group` 的影响。
360	
361	**操作步骤**（待本地验证；只需 `pypdf`，无需 img2pdf/GPU）：
362	
363	1. 在仓库根目录之外新建 `estimate_demo.py`（示例代码）：
364	
365	   ```python
366	   import glob
367	   import math
368	   import random
369	
370	   from pypdf import PdfReader
371	
372	   files = glob.glob("<仓库路径>/tests/gnarly_pdfs/*.pdf")

382	
383	   avg = sum(page_counts) / len(page_counts)
384	   for target in (500, 50):
385	       ipg = max(1, int(target / avg))
386	       print(f"avg_pages={avg:.2f}  target={target}  items_per_group={ipg}")
387	   ```
388	
389	2. 把 `<仓库路径>` 替换为本机仓库位置，运行 `python estimate_demo.py`。
390	
391	**需要观察的现象**：打印出的 `avg_pages`（gnarly_pdfs 是人工挑选的疑难样本，页数分布可能与真实语料不同）；同一均值下目标 500 与 50 得到的 `items_per_group` 成约 10 倍关系。

393	**预期结果**：`avg_pages` 为某个正数（具体值待本地验证，不同 PDF 集合结果不同）；两组 `items_per_group` 均为不小于 1 的整数。可再删掉 `random.sample` 改为全量统计，对比样本均值与真实均值的偏差，体会 100 上限的抽样误差有多大。

396	
397	**练习 1**：采样循环对每个样本都要 `get_s3_bytes` 完整下载一次文件。`pypdf` 数页数其实只需要 PDF 的交叉引用表（文件尾部）。查看 [s3_utils.py:L87-L105](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/s3_utils.py#L87-L105) 的函数签名，说明代码已为这种优化预留了什么能力、为什么这里没用。

417	
418	**预期结果**：日志计数与你准备的文件数一致；索引中能看到图片路径与 tarball 路径并存。若想再进一步，可把 `--pages_per_group 20` 显式传入，观察 `items_per_group` 随目标页数线性变化。（步骤 3、4 待本地验证。）
419	
420	## 6. 本讲小结
421	
422	- `--pdfs` 的五种输入形态（S3 路径/glob、本地 PDF、本地图片、本地 tarball、txt 清单）经分类后**殊途同归**到两个集合：单文档路径集 `pdf_work_paths` 与 tarball 集 `tarball_paths`，集合用 `set` 天然去重。
423	- 本地文件走「后缀白名单 + 魔数」双重校验（`%PDF` 4 字节、PNG 8 字节、JPEG 2 字节）；S3 glob 展开只按后缀分 tarball，完整性校验推迟到 worker 取到字节之后。
424	- 图片输入不在收集时转换，而在 `process_pdf` 下载后经 `is_png`/`is_jpeg` 二次探测、由 `convert_image_to_pdf_bytes`（外部命令 `img2pdf`，**不在 pip 依赖中**）包成单页 PDF，从而免费复用整套「按页处理」机制。

# 输入收集：本地路径、S3 glob、tarball 与图片转 PDF

## 1. 本讲目标

上一讲我们俯瞰了 `main()` 的十个检查点，知道它「先搭台、再派活、最后收场」。本讲放大第一个真正的业务检查点——**输入收集**：`--pdfs` 参数里那些五花八门的路径，是如何被整理成一份干净的工作清单的。

学完本讲你应该能够：

1. 逐分支描述 `--pdfs` 支持的五种输入形态（S3 路径/glob、本地 PDF、本地图片、本地 tarball、txt 路径清单）以及它们的处理分支与错误分支。
2. 解释 PNG/JPEG 魔数（magic number）检测的原理，说明 olmOCR 为什么「不信后缀、信文件头」，以及一张图片是如何在流水线里被包成单页 PDF 的。
3. 掌握「采样估算平均页数 → 计算 `items_per_group`」的逻辑，理解为什么分组粒度要按**页数**而不是按**文档个数**来定。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 魔数（magic number）

文件的后缀名是可以随便改的：把 `photo.png` 改名成 `photo.pdf`，文件内容一个字节都不会变。所以判断文件真实类型的可靠办法，是读文件开头的几个字节——几乎所有文件格式都在开头约定了一串「签名字节」，俗称魔数：

| 格式 | 开头字节（Python 字节串表示） | 长度 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| PNG | `b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"` | 8 字节 |
| JPEG | `b"\xff\xd8"`（SOI 段标记） | 2 字节 |
| PDF | `b"%PDF"` | 4 字节 |

本讲会看到 olmOCR 对同一路径做了**后缀 + 魔数**的双重校验：后缀决定「要不要看」，魔数决定「算不算数」。

### 2.2 glob 模式

glob 是 shell 风格的通配符匹配：`*` 匹配任意字符序列，`?` 匹配单个字符，`[abc]` 匹配方括号内任一字符。`s3://bucket/pdfs/*.pdf` 的含义就是「该 bucket 下 pdfs 前缀里所有以 `.pdf` 结尾的对象」。S3 本身不支持通配符查询，所以代码需要先算出通配符之前的最长固定前缀，用前缀列举对象，再在客户端逐个做 glob 匹配。

### 2.3 tarball 与 `tarball::内部路径` 记法

tarball 指打包压缩文件（这里是 `.tar.gz` / `.tgz`）。olmOCR 允许把成百上千个 PDF 打成一个 tarball 交给流水线，用它自己的记法 `tarball路径::内部成员路径`（注意是**双冒号**）来指称「某个 tarball 里的某个 PDF」，例如 `s3://bucket/batch1.tar.gz::docs/paper.pdf`。这样做的好处是：百万个小文件在 S3 上列举、请求的开销都很大，合并成大对象能显著降低请求成本。

### 2.4 采样估计与「按页分组」

设文档总数为 \( N \)，每篇文档的页数为 \( p_i \)。逐篇数页太贵（要把所有 PDF 都下载一遍），于是随机抽 \( n = \min(100, N) \) 篇，用样本均值

\[ \bar{p} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i \]

估计全体平均页数，再换算出每个工作项（work item group）应装多少篇文档。直觉是：**流水线真正的工作量以「页」为单位**（每页要渲染一次、推理一次），一个组装 5 篇 200 页的大书和装 5 篇 1 页的传单，工作量差了两个数量级。按页数定组大小，能让每个 work item 的工作量大致均匀，从而断点续跑的粒度均匀、重试的代价可控。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

| 文件 | 本讲涉及范围 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [olmocr/pipeline.py](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py) | L1334-L1412 输入收集主段；L479-L482 tarball 判定；L575-L599 图片转 PDF 的下游消费；L1205-L1210 参数定义 | 输入分类、采样估算、入队 |
| [olmocr/image_utils.py](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/image_utils.py) | 全文（仅 61 行） | 魔数探测与图片转 PDF |
| [olmocr/s3_utils.py](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/s3_utils.py) | L36-L63 glob 展开；L87-L98 本地/S3 统一取字节 | 输入收集的底层取数工具 |

辅助背景（本讲只引用不展开）：`olmocr/work_queue.py` 的 `populate_queue`（下一单元 u3-l1 精读）、`pyproject.toml` 的依赖清单（确认 `img2pdf` 并非 pip 依赖）。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 输入分类分支：五种输入形态，两个归宿

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`--pdfs` 是 `nargs="*"` 的可变参数，一次可以跟很多个值，每个值独立走一遍分类逻辑。分类的目标不是「给每个文件贴标签」，而是把所有输入**归并到两个集合**里：

- `pdf_work_paths`：单文档路径（本地路径或 `s3://` 路径，PDF 或图片混装）；
- `tarball_paths`：tarball 路径，每个 tarball 后续会被当成**一个**工作项整体处理。

为什么是这两个集合？因为下游的处理方式完全不同：普通 PDF 按采样算出的 `items_per_group` 分组入队；tarball 不拆分、一个 tarball 就是一个工作项（`populate_queue(tarball_paths, 1)`）。分组的语义（组哈希、done flag、断点续跑）在 u3-l1 会展开，这里只需记住「集合决定命运」。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

对 `args.pdfs` 中的每个值，依次判断：

```text
对每个 pdf_path:
  ├─ 以 "s3://" 开头?
  │    └─ 是 → expand_s3_glob 展开成具体对象集合
  │             ├─ 是 tarball 后缀 → tarball_paths
  │             └─ 其他           → pdf_work_paths
  ├─ 本地存在?
  │    ├─ 是 tarball 后缀 → tarball_paths
  │    ├─ 后缀是 .pdf/.png/.jpg/.jpeg (不区分大小写):
  │    │    ├─ 开头 4 字节 == b"%PDF"      → pdf_work_paths (按 PDF 装载)
  │    │    ├─ is_png() 或 is_jpeg() 为真  → pdf_work_paths (按图片装载)
  │    │    └─ 否则 → 打 warning, 跳过该文件
  │    ├─ 后缀是 .txt → 逐行读路径, 每行再按 tarball 与否分流到两个集合
  │    └─ 其他后缀 → raise ValueError
  └─ 都不是 → raise ValueError("pdfs argument needs to be either a local path,
                                 an s3 path, or an s3 glob pattern...")
最终: pdf_work_paths 采样分组入队; tarball_paths 以 1 个/项入队
```

注意两个细节：

1. **txt 清单是「递归一层」的展开**：清单里每行可以是一个普通路径，也可以是一个 tarball，代码对每行再次调用 `is_tarball_path` 分流；
2. **S3 分支没有后缀白名单**：glob 展开出什么就收什么（只区分 tarball 与否），校验责任交给了 glob 模式本身；而本地分支有严格的后缀 + 魔数双重校验。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

先看参数定义。[pipeline.py:L1205-L1210](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1205-L1210) 用 `nargs="*"` 声明 `--pdfs`，帮助文本明确列出三种典型用法（S3 glob、清单文件等）：

```python
parser.add_argument(
    "--pdfs",
    nargs="*",
    help="Path to add pdfs stored in s3 to the workspace, can be a glob path s3://bucket/prefix/*.pdf or path to file containing list of pdf paths",
    default=None,
)
```

主分类逻辑在 [pipeline.py:L1334-L1373](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1334-L1373)。这段代码先初始化两个集合，然后进入 for 循环：

- [pipeline.py:L1341-L1345](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1341-L1345)：S3 分支。`expand_s3_glob(pdf_s3, pdf_path)` 把 glob 展开为 `{'s3://bucket/key': etag}` 字典，随后用两个推导式按 `is_tarball_path` 分流到两个集合。
- [pipeline.py:L1346-L1363](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1346-L1363)：本地分支。先判 tarball，再用 `lower().endswith(...)` 判四种后缀；关键一行是 `open(pdf_path, "rb").read(4) == b"%PDF"`——**直接读 4 个字节和 PDF 魔数比对**。后缀对但魔数不对时，再退而求其次问 `is_png`/`is_jpeg`（处理「实际是图片却顶着 .pdf 后缀」的文件）；两者都不是只打 warning 跳过，不中断整个任务。
- [pipeline.py:L1364-L1369](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1364-L1369)：txt 清单分支。逐行 `strip()` 并丢弃空行，每行同样按 tarball 与否分流。
- [pipeline.py:L1370-L1373](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1370-L1373)：两个错误分支——本地存在但后缀不支持 → `ValueError`；本地不存在（且不是 s3://）→ `ValueError`。

tarball 的判定标准非常朴素，见 [pipeline.py:L479-L482](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L479-L482)：只看小写后缀是不是 `.tar.gz` 或 `.tgz`（这里没有魔数校验）：


### 4.2 图片格式探测与图片转 PDF

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

olmOCR 的推理单元是「PDF 的一页」——渲染成图片交给视觉语言模型（u2-l3 会精读渲染）。既然模型看到的本来就是图片，那直接吃 PNG/JPEG 岂不更直接？流水线仍选择**先把图片包成单页 PDF**，理由是统一内部表示：下游所有环节（按页处理、页码元数据、Dolma 的 `pdf_page_spans`、断点重试）都建立在「文档 = 若干页」的抽象上。把图片包装成 1 页 PDF，就能让图片输入免费复用整套 PDF 机制，而不是在几十处代码里写 `if 图片` 分支。

负责这件事的是 `olmocr/image_utils.py`，三个函数各司其职：`is_png`/`is_jpeg` 探测格式，`convert_image_to_pdf_bytes` 完成转换。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

转换本身不重写 PDF 编码，而是调用外部命令行工具 `img2pdf`（「无损嵌入」：图片字节被直接放进 PDF 容器，不二次压缩）：

```text
convert_image_to_pdf_bytes(路径或路径列表)
  ├─ 输入归一化: str → [str]; 空列表 → ValueError
  ├─ 逐个检查文件存在, 不存在 → ValueError
  ├─ subprocess.run(["img2pdf", 文件...], capture_output=True)
  │    ├─ 成功 → 返回 stdout (即 PDF 字节)
  │    └─ CalledProcessError → 抛 RuntimeError(携带 stderr)
```

在流水线中的消费时机（不是收集时立刻转，而是**worker 取到文件时**才转）：

```text
process_pdf(pdf_orig_path)
  ├─ get_s3_bytes_with_backoff 下载字节到临时文件 (本地路径则直接读盘)
  ├─ is_png(tf.name) 或 is_jpeg(tf.name)?
  │    └─ 是 → tf.seek(0); 重写为 convert_image_to_pdf_bytes(tf.name) 的输出
  └─ process_single_pdf(...)  # 此时临时文件一定是合法 PDF
```

```python
            header = f.read(8)
            return header == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error: {e}")
        return False

def is_jpeg(file_path):
    try:

            header = f.read(2)
            return header == b"\xff\xd8"
    ...
```

此外，采样循环里也复用了同一对探测器：[pipeline.py:L1390-L1391](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1390-L1391) 把图片直接记为 1 页——一张图片就是一页文档，参与平均页数的计算。

### 4.3 pages_per_group 采样估算：按页定组

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

回忆 u1-l5：`--pages_per_group` 用 `argparse.SUPPRESS` 声明、无静态默认值，在 [pipeline.py:L1314-L1315](https://github.com/allenai/olmocr/blob/f7cfe4c22098b154c76b6ec950d1c0a464eecf8d/olmocr/pipeline.py#L1314-L1315) 按运行形态补默认：走外部计费 API（给了 `--api_key`）时目标是每组约 **50** 页，自有 GPU 时 **500** 页。本模块讲这个「目标页数」如何变成「每组文档数」。

为什么按页分组（2.4 节的直觉再推一步）：一个 work item group 是断点续跑与完成标记的最小单元（u3-l1），组的工作量 = 组内总页数。若按固定文档数分组，遇到「1000 页的大书 + 1 页的收据」混合语料，组工作量会相差三个数量级：大组失败重试代价高、done flag 粒度太粗；小组则索引条目爆炸。控制「每组页数恒定」→ 每组重试代价上限恒定、进度统计均匀。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```text
若 pdf_work_paths 非空:
  n = min(100, 文档总数)
  sampled = random.sample(pdf_work_paths, n)        # 均匀随机抽样
  for pdf in sampled:
    字节 = get_s3_bytes(pdf_s3, pdf)                 # 本地路径直接读盘, s3 路径走网络
    写入临时文件
    if is_png 或 is_jpeg: 页数 = 1
    else:               页数 = len(PdfReader(临时文件).pages)
    读取失败 → warning 并跳过 (不中断)
  平均页数 p̄ = sum(页数) / len(页数)   # 全部失败 → 兜底 p̄ = 10
  items_per_group = max(1, int(pages_per_group / p̄))
  populate_queue(pdf_work_paths, items_per_group)
```

换算公式（`int()` 即向零取整，也就是正数域的下取整 \(\lfloor\cdot\rfloor\)）：

\[ \text{items\_per\_group} = \max\left(1,\ \left\lfloor \frac{\text{pages\_per\_group}}{\bar{p}} \right\rfloor\right) \]

几个边界：样本上限 100（再多的抽样收益递减，而每个样本都要下载一次文件）；单次读取失败只 warning 不中断（脏数据在大规模语料中是常态）；`max(1, ...)` 保证平均页数超过目标页数（比如全是 600 页的大书、目标 500 页）时，每组至少仍装 1 篇——宁可组偏大，也不能出现空组。

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a message from the system confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a message from the system confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.
